predecessors.name: Saadi Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Middle Atlas highlands around Dila, then 'large parts of northern Morocco' conquered from 1637

successors.name: Morocco
successors.text: the Dila'ite lands of central and northern Morocco until 1668, 'when Dila itself was annexed by the 'Alawites after their initial conquest of Fez'

rulers.name: Mohammed al-Hajj
rulers.title: head of the zawiya, Sultan of Morocco 1659-1663

ledger.x: 1637: the Zawiya of Dila rebels against the Saadis.
1641: the Dila'ites hold Meknes and Fez.
1659: Mohammed al-Hajj is proclaimed Sultan of Morocco at Fez.
1662: Fez is lost to a putsch.

wars.name: Dila'iya conquest of northern Morocco
wars.outcome: From 1637 the brotherhood conquered large parts of northern Morocco and by 1641 held Meknes, Fez and Salé; the Saadi family was expelled from Fez and Mohammed al-Hajj proclaimed Sultan.

wars.name: Fez's revolt of 1651
wars.outcome: 'In 1651, Fez rebelled and invited Muhammad ibn Sharif, but Mohammed al-Hajj forced its submission.'

wars.name: Loss of Salé and Fez
wars.outcome: Salé rose against the Dila'ite governor in 1660 and was lost in 1661; Fez was lost in 1662 after the putsch of Qaid Al-Doraidi; in 1663 Mohammed al-Hajj declined the appeal of Fez's leaders and retreated to the highland capital.

wars.name: Alawite conquest of the Dila'iya
wars.outcome: Al-Rashid 'secured the surrender of Fez in June 1666', 'destroyed their capital in the Middle Atlas in June 1668' and captured Marrakesh in July; the Dila'ite family was exiled to Tlemcen.

certainty.note: A brotherhood's domain, with towns held and tribes in between: no page gives a frontier.
